title: Analog inputs and outputs
summary: Analog signals carry a value, not just on/off: 4-20 mA, 0-20 mA or 0-10 V. The module converts the signal into an integer (raw value) that the program scales into engineering units.

sections.heading: From signal to number
sections.body:
An analog input module measures a current or voltage and converts it into an integer, the **raw value**. Each vendor uses its own representation. Examples:

| Platform style | Nominal range of the raw value |
| --- | --- |
| Siemens S7-1200/S7-1500 | 0 to 27648 for the nominal signal range |
| Beckhoff EL305x (default presentation) | 0 (4 mA) to 32767 (20 mA) |
| PLC Lab generic profile | 0 to 10000 (= 0 to 100 %) |

The program must **scale** the raw value into the physical unit (%, bar, litres).

sections.heading: Over- and underrange
sections.body: Signals slightly outside the nominal range are still converted (**overrange/underrange**). Far outside, the module reports **overflow/underflow** with special values and, if diagnostics are enabled, a diagnostic event. With 4-20 mA inputs a current far below 4 mA is detected as **wire break**.

sections.heading: Configuration matters
sections.body: Each analog channel is configured for a measurement type (for example *current 4-20 mA* or *voltage 0-10 V*). A channel configured as 0-20 mA while the transmitter delivers 4-20 mA reads a value about 20 % too high at the bottom of the range: a frequent commissioning error.

facts.label: S7-1500 nominal analog range
facts.value: 0 to 27648 (bipolar ranges -27648 to 27648); overrange up to 32511, overflow 32767 - check the module manual
